answer: Each agent proves its identity per round with a sequential, memory-hard proof: 2^27 chained hashes walking a 2 GB canyon of RAM, seeded by the epoch beacon so nothing can be precomputed, and due by the zenith block mid-epoch. An honest agent spends about 3 CPU-minutes; 1,000 sybils need 1,000 machines with 2 GB each running in parallel every round. Verifiers recheck 64 random steps; one bad step burns the account's stake. Colluders cannot pool work, since each proof binds to one key and the serial chain cannot be split across helpers.
